title: Philips FMVDemo reverse scan shows black macroblock regions
symptom: Using the Play Control panel's backward-scan function produces transient black rectangular regions aligned to MPEG block boundaries while the surrounding video remains visible.
expected: Determine whether real VMPEG reverse scan displays complete GOP entry pictures or exposes comparable transient decoder artifacts; do not conceal the blocks without hardware evidence.

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: FMVDemo reverse scan jumps backward among authored SOS/GOP entry points. The emulator may present a picture before all required reference or slice state for that newly selected GOP is valid, leaving macroblock-aligned black regions.
supporting_evidence: The artifacts are rectangular and aligned to MPEG macroblock-sized regions.
Philips play_control.c states that backward scan jumps among entry points where every twelfth encoded frame is preceded by SOS and GOP codes.
Normal forward playback does not retain the same black rectangles.
contradicting_evidence: No decoder-error or selected-entry diagnostic was captured with the screenshot.
Real VMPEG hardware may expose transient coarse or incomplete pictures during reverse scan.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Trace each reverse entry point, sequence/GOP/picture headers, decoder reference reset, slice coverage, and presented raster. Complete slice coverage and valid reference state before presentation would falsify this explanation.

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The cartridge's scan mode may intentionally prioritize rapid GOP stepping over a clean continuous picture, making transient incomplete-looking frames authentic hardware behavior.
supporting_evidence: The sample source describes scan as sparse GOP-entry playback rather than reverse decoding of every frame.
No real-hardware comparison is currently available.
contradicting_evidence: Large black macroblock regions ordinarily indicate missing or invalid decoded content rather than merely low temporal resolution.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Capture the same FMVDemo backward-scan sequence from a real 22ER9141 VMPEG cartridge. Clean complete pictures on hardware would falsify the authored/native explanation.

manual_verification.notes: A 768x574 diagnostic screenshot with SHA-256 ee0bcd5cb40d4508670a96a20fd87fa61417ce4b09738650418513b43aabeb7d captures black block-aligned regions during FMVDemo backward scan. The image remains local and untracked. Hardware correctness is unknown.
